claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC dendritic high-entropy alloy.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a low-temperature yield strength of about 800 MPa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline high-temperature result involves 30% compressive strain.
A fine, uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles should be incorporated into TiVNbTa using an adapted powder-metallurgy consolidation process.
Y2O3 dispersoids are thermally stable at the relevant elevated temperatures.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as pinning points that impede dislocation motion.
The Y2O3 dispersion restricts grain-boundary sliding.
The oxide dispersion helps preserve a refined microstructure at 1273 K.
Suppressing dislocation motion, creep, and grain-boundary sliding will increase the alloy's elevated-temperature yield strength.
At 1273 K, oxide-dispersion-strengthened TiVNbTa will have a yield strength greater than the approximately 330 MPa baseline.
The yield-strength improvement at 1273 K may range from tens of MPa to approximately 200 MPa.
The modified alloy may retain approximately 30% strain capacity at 1273 K.
The proposed intervention is intended for operation around 1273 K and mechanical strain regimes up to 30–40%.
Achieving a uniform dispersoid distribution may be difficult and may affect the magnitude of strengthening and retained ductility.
The thermal-expansion compatibility of the modified alloy with W and CuCrZr remains unvalidated.
